nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of `hasDerivAt_freeEnergy`, on a convex open time set `I` the free energy is nonincreasing.
nodes.title: Free-energy decay

nodes.summary: Rotational drifts share the Gibbs stationary density (non-identifiability): for a `C²` potential `Ψ`, `D ≠ 0` and an antisymmetric matrix `A` (`Aᵀ = -A`), the drift `-(∇Ψ + A ∇Ψ)` satisfies `div J = 0` for `p = e^{-Ψ / D}`.
nodes.title: Rotational drifts share the Gibbs stationary density

nodes.summary: The divergence `div F (x) = ∑ᵢ ∂ᵢ Fᵢ (x)` of a vector field.
nodes.title: Divergence of a vector field

nodes.summary: Two differentiable potentials whose gradient drifts both have zero flux for the same positive differentiable density differ by a constant.
nodes.title: Identifiability of the potential

nodes.summary: An explicit rotational drift with nonzero flux (our derivation): on `ℝ²` with `Ψ(x) = (x₀² + x₁²) / 2`, `D = 1` and the rotation generator `A = [[0, 1], [-1, 0]]`, the drift `-(∇Ψ + A ∇Ψ)` has the Gibbs (standard Gaussian, up to normalization) density as a stationary density, yet its flux at `(1, 0)` is nonzero, so it is not the gradient drift.
nodes.title: An explicit rotational drift with nonzero flux

nodes.summary: The Gibbs density has zero flux under the gradient drift `-∇Ψ`: for differentiable `Ψ`, `D ≠ 0` and any constant `c`, `J = -∇Ψ · c e^{-Ψ/D} - D ∇(c e^{-Ψ/D}) = 0`.
nodes.title: The Gibbs density has zero flux

nodes.summary: The flux of the Gibbs density under the drift `-(∇Ψ + A ∇Ψ)` is the rotational part `-(A ∇Ψ) e^{-Ψ / D}` (for differentiable `Ψ`, `D ≠ 0`, any matrix `A`).
nodes.title: Flux of the Gibbs density under a rotational gradient drift

nodes.summary: The probability flux `J = b p - D ∇p` of the diffusion `dX = b dt + √(2D) dW` with density `p`.
nodes.title: Probability flux of a diffusion

nodes.summary: The Gibbs density is stationary for the gradient drift: `-div J = 0`.
nodes.title: The Gibbs density is stationary

nodes.summary: The Fokker–Planck operator `-div J`: the density evolves by `∂ₜ p = fokkerPlanckOp D b p`, and `p` is stationary iff this vanishes.
nodes.title: Fokker–Planck operator

nodes.summary: The free energy `F(t) = ∫ₐᵇ (Ψ p + D p log p) dx` of the density `p(t, ·)` on `[a, b]` (potential `Ψ`, diffusion coefficient `D`).
nodes.title: Free energy of a Fokker–Planck density
Gradient of a function on Euclidean coordinate space

nodes.summary: Let `p` be `C²` in `(t, x)`, positive for times in an open set `I`, and solve the no-flux gradient-drift Fokker–Planck equation on `[a, b]` for `t ∈ I`, with `C²` potential `Ψ` (any real `D`). Then for `t ∈ I`, `F'(t) = -∫ₐᵇ p (Ψ' + D ∂ₓ log p)² dx`. Only the values of `p` on `[a, b]` enter `F`; positivity is asked of the whole `C²` function `p t` so that `log (p t)` is `C²`.
nodes.title: Dissipation identity

nodes.summary: If `p` is `C²` and solves the no-flux equation on `[a, b]` for times in `I` (positivity is not needed), the total mass `∫ₐᵇ p(t, x) dx` has zero time derivative at every `t ∈ I`.
nodes.title: Mass conservation

nodes.summary: `p` solves the gradient-drift Fokker–Planck equation `∂ₜ p = ∂ₓ (p Ψ' + D ∂ₓ p)` on `[a, b]` with zero flux at both ends, for times `t ∈ I`.
nodes.title: No-flux solution of the gradient-drift Fokker–Planck equation

nodes.summary: The (negative) probability flux `p Ψ' + D ∂ₓ p` of the gradient-drift Fokker–Planck equation at `(t, x)`; the flux itself is `-(p Ψ' + D ∂ₓ p)`.
nodes.title: Negative probability flux of the Fokker–Planck equation

nodes.summary: If `p > 0` is differentiable and the gradient drift `-∇Ψ` has zero flux for `p`, then `∂ᵢ Ψ = -D ∂ᵢ log p`.
nodes.title: A zero-flux density determines the drift

nodes.summary: The partial derivative `∂ᵢ f (x) = Df(x) eᵢ` on `Fin n → ℝ`.
nodes.title: Partial derivative on Euclidean coordinate space

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
